final.memo:
We have reviewed the Company and have decided to pass. Charlie and I prefer to invest in businesses where we understand the economics and can rely on the integrity of management [D05]. In this case, significant workplace allegations and compensation controversies raise fundamental questions about the company's culture and the stability of its creative engine [D01, D05, D07].

Unlike the wonderful businesses we seek, this company relies on constant creative investment, which complicates our ability to forecast long-term owner earnings [D01]. We do not engage in turnarounds, and when management credibility is in question, the risk of permanent loss of capital is simply too high [D05].

Given our $144.1 billion cash position, we have no shortage of opportunities that fit our criteria without requiring us to speculate on a complex cultural recovery [D08]. We prefer to wait for businesses that meet our high standards for durability and management honesty [D08].
